name: adduction hand with elbow extended stretch
interpretation: Anatomical left arm extends in front, slightly across the midline, with the shoulder down and a naturally near-straight elbow. Its palm stays vertical, thumb side above little-finger side. The assisting right hand approaches from above, closes an articulated gentle overhand grasp and guides an 18-degree little-finger-side wrist tilt in the palm plane. This is ulnar deviation, rather than wrist flexion. The left hand returns to neutral and the assist opens and releases. The compressed five-second demonstration is separate from the source 20–30-second workout hold. Mirror the complete motion to repeat on the right. No bouncing or phase-dependent recruitment claim.

authored_choices.side: Left; mirror for the other side.
authored_choices.timing: 0–1.05 s grasp acquisition; 1.05–2 s ulnar tilt; 2–3 s quiet hold; 3–5 s exact reversed release.
authored_choices.stance: Original standing pelvis, trunk, legs and bilateral feet remain fixed.
authored_choices.source_locked_elbow_interpretation: Naturally near-straight; no hyperextension. Measured internal elbow angle is recorded in surface-contact-report.json.
authored_choices.hand_mechanic: Thumb-up vertical palm; hand direction tilts toward the lower little-finger edge while its palm-plane normal stays lateral.
authored_choices.assist: Right hand uses all 15 original finger bones; thumb, index and middle contact proximity is checked against actual left-hand triangles throughout the entry and hold.
authored_choices.angle_status: Reversible illustration values, no clinical target or measured recruitment.
authored_choices.muscle_display: Soft cyan zones on selected anatomical-left forearm proxies only; wrist flexor/extensor fields are anatomical proxies. Right assist and hand intrinsic muscles stay neutral. Runtime fields are primary-owned.
authored_choices.runtime_skin: Original four-influence linear binding, no weight edits, morphs or DQ. CorrectiveSmooth and Multires disabled in the canonical source and GLB.
authored_choices.cameras: Two complementary whole-body orthographic obliques. Primary may fit final horizontal width.

instructions: Stand tall and extend one arm in front of you with the elbow straight.
Turn the palm so the thumb points up.
Grab the hand with your other hand and tilt it gently toward the little finger side.
Keep the elbow locked and the shoulder down.
Release and repeat on the other arm.
